rows.question: What is the exposure dial's rule?
rows.answer: Afternoon, sir. The dial is OPEN (buying allowed) when Bitcoin's daily close is above both its 50-day average and its 200-day average. If either one fails, it closes: no new buys and cash is the position. Right now Bitcoin closed at about 83 thousand, above the 50-day at about 80.7 thousand and the 200-day at about 72.7 thousand, so it's open. Want the evidence behind it?

rows.question: Which daily rule has a measured edge, and in which market state?
rows.answer: Afternoon, sir. Only one daily rule has a measured edge: the short dip trade (H07), on tier-A coins while the exposure dial is CLOSED. It earned about 5 percent a trade over random after costs, in both test periods. Right now the dial is OPEN, so that cell isn't live today, and nothing else has a measured edge.

rows.question: How many coins do you watch live across the market?
rows.answer: Afternoon, sir. I watch about 393 coins live: every coin trading against USDT on Binance. They're split into tier A (big, over $20M a day), tier B (mid-size) and tier C (small, watched only, never judged). Ten of them, Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, Cardano, Dogecoin, Avalanche, Bitcoin Cash, Chainlink, Litecoin and XRP, also get the 15-minute Explorer scan. Want me to show which coins moved most today?

rows.question: What did review 27 find about stops on dip buys?
need: no stop|without a stop|time exit|exit by time|time only
rows.answer: Good afternoon, sir. Review 27 found that dip buys do best with no stop and a 10-day time exit. On 120 coins, the short dip trade with no stop earned about 6.5% a trade in 2018-23 and about 2.4% in 2024-26. With a tight stop it earned only about half a percent in both periods. The trade works by riding out the dip, so a stop sells you out before the bounce. Two limits: the measured edge is only for big tier-A coins while the dial is closed, and the dial is open today. A plain 200-day touch loses with every exit. I've opened the Evidence page so you can see it. Want me to walk through how the b

rows.question: What is the benchmark every strategy must beat?
rows.answer: Afternoon, sir. The benchmark every strategy must beat is GATE50: hold coins only while Bitcoin is above its 50-day average, and sit in cash otherwise. It's the simple rule a strategy has to beat after costs, or it isn't adding anything. The market is open right now, with Bitcoin about 2.9% above that average.

rows.question: Did tuning the deep-dip buy E6 in review 24 work?
rows.answer: Afternoon, sir. No, it didn't work. Review 24 failed: none of the E6 variants made money after costs in either period. The plain deep-dip buy does beat random entries, but by too little to pay the fee and spread.

rows.question: What fee per side do we assume on NDAX?
rows.answer: Afternoon, sir. We assume 0.20% per side on NDAX, plus the measured spread on top. For coins outside the lab 10, we assume a 0.40% spread. So a round trip costs roughly 0.4% in fees before the spread. That's why most of our short-term ideas lost money: costs ate the edge.

rows.question: How much of the book does one setup trade risk in the 500 dollar book?
rows.answer: Afternoon, sir. In the $500 book, each setup trade risks 0.5% of the book, which is about $2.50 if the stop is hit. No single trade can be bigger than 10% of the book, so about $50 in position size. Total risk across all open trades is capped at 6%, about $30.

rows.question: What daily loss stops new buys in the 500 dollar book?
rows.answer: Afternoon, sir. A 2% loss in one day stops new buys in the $500 book. That's the day brake, and it hasn't fired. The week brake is 4%, the losing-streak brake is 4 losses in a row, and a 15% fall from the peak pauses the book until you resume it. The book is at about $492 CAD, down 1.5% since Oct 11. It holds only Bitcoin and Ethereum and has no closed trades yet. It passes 2 of 10 graduation gates, so it isn't ready. Want me to walk through the graduation gates?

rows.question: What happens if the 500 dollar book falls 15% from its peak?
rows.answer: Afternoon, sir. A 15% fall from its peak is a hard stop. The $500 book is paused, and it stays paused until you resume it yourself. It doesn't restart on its own. The book is nowhere near that now. It's worth about $492, down 1.5%, and no brake has fired. The smaller brakes come first: 2% in a day, 4% in a week, or 4 losses in a row. Today the book holds Bitcoin and Ethereum, because the exposure dial is open. It has no closed trades yet, and it passes 2 of 10 graduation checks, so it's not ready for real money. Want me to walk through how the smaller brakes work?

rows.question: How many losing trades in a row pause buying?
rows.answer: Afternoon, sir. Four losses in a row pause buying. That's one of the brakes on the $500 account book. The others are a 2% loss in a day, 4% in a week, and a 15% fall in the book. Once any brake fires, buying stays paused until you resume it.

rows.question: What does the core sleeve of the 500 dollar book hold?
rows.answer: Afternoon, sir. The core sleeve holds Bitcoin and Ethereum, bought on Oct 11 when the dial opened. Bitcoin is about $200 CAD, 40% of the book, and Ethereum is about $100 CAD, 20%. Both are slightly under water: Bitcoin is down from about 118,500 to 116,700, and Ethereum from about 3,570 to 3,430. The whole book is worth about $492, down 1.5%. The remaining $199 is cash, and the other sleeves hold nothing yet.

rows.question: Which exchange is the 500 dollar book built for?
rows.answer: Afternoon, sir. The $500 book is built for NDAX, in Canadian dollars. Its paper fills are checked against NDAX's bid and ask, and costs are NDAX's 0.20% fee plus the spread. It's paper only, with no exchange connected, so nothing real can be ordered yet. Want me to pull up the book?

rows.question: How many trigger points does an Explorer setup give the brain now?
rows.answer: Afternoon, sir. Zero. Since the repair-shop change on Oct 21, an Explorer setup gives the brain no trigger points. The Explorer is rejected as a trading book, so it never wakes the brain by itself.

rows.question: What daily trading volume puts a coin in tier A?
rows.answer: Afternoon, sir. Tier A is any coin trading over $20 million a day. Tier B is $1 million to $20 million, and tier C is under $1 million. We watch tier C but never judge it.

rows.question: What do you hold when the dial is closed?
rows.answer: Afternoon, sir. When the dial is closed, the $500 book holds mostly cash. The core sleeve (Bitcoin and Ethereum) goes to cash. The only things allowed are the short dip trade on big tier-A coins, up to 30% of the book, and my own judgment buys, up to 10%. Right now the dial is open, so it's holding the core: Bitcoin and Ethereum, with about $200 CAD in cash.

rows.question: What is the H07 entry?
rows.answer: Good afternoon, sir. The H07 entry is a daily signal. The coin's 10-day RSI, a gauge of how stretched the price is, closes under 30 while the coin is still above its 200-day average. We buy $100 at the next price. There's no stop. We exit when RSI is back over 40, or after 10 days at most. One thing matters right now. Its measured edge is only on big tier-A coins while the exposure dial is closed. The dial is open today, so the evidence there is thin and H07 isn't a proven trade in this state.

rows.question: What is Madhav's M1 setup?
rows.answer: Afternoon, sir. M1 is your capitulation-at-the-lows setup, the one modeled on your June 5 Solana buy: a sharp sell-off where many give up at once, and you buy near the bottom. History didn't back it as a buy signal on its own (review #5). On the 2018-2023 data it did no better than a random day, because the 2022 capitulations kept falling. So it marks a place to look, not a reason to buy.

rows.question: How many coins are in the research lake?
rows.answer: Afternoon, sir. The research lake holds 120 coins. 93 are still listed and the rest are delisted or stopped. We keep the dead ones in so the history isn't flattered by survivors only. 54 of the 120 trade against CAD on NDAX. They sit at three levels: 10 watched live all day, 30 in the paper tier, and the rest research only. Separately, the live market watch covers about 393 coins. I've opened Markets for you.

rows.question: Is the hourly watch running?
rows.answer: Afternoon, sir. No, the hourly watch is parked. You decided that on Oct 11, after it made only 2 setups in 12 days. Its code is kept, but it isn't scanning now. Hunter's book is frozen at 22 trades: 3 wins, 19 losses, down about $32.51.

rows.question: What will Bitcoin's price be on December 31, 2026?
rows.answer: Afternoon, sir. I can't tell you Bitcoin's price on December 31, and nobody honestly can. Bitcoin is about 84.5 thousand dollars now, up about two percent today. My written view only covers the next few days: chop between roughly 80 and 85 thousand. I'd change that view if Bitcoin closes under its 50-day average, about 80.7 thousand, or above 85 thousand on broad strength.

rows.question: Will Ethereum beat Solana next month?
rows.answer: Afternoon, sir. I can't tell you that, and nothing we've tested gives an edge on it. Today ETH is up about two and a half percent and SOL about one and three-quarters, and both sit below their 50-day averages. If I had to lean, it's a coin flip, so I wouldn't build a trade on it.

rows.question: What did review 40 find?
rows.answer: Good afternoon, sir. There is no review 40 yet, so it hasn't found anything. The repair board holds 38 reviews, and the newest is number 38. I'm opening the Evidence page for you now.

rows.question: On what exact date will the next Bitcoin crash start?
rows.answer: Afternoon, sir. I can't give you that date, and nobody honestly can. Nothing in our data predicts the start of a crash. What I can do is tell you what would flip us to cash: a Bitcoin daily close under its 50-day average, about 80,700 dollars. Bitcoin is at about 84,500 now, so it's roughly 4.5% above that line.

rows.question: Which coin will rise the most tomorrow?
rows.answer: Afternoon, sir. I can't tell you which coin will rise most tomorrow, and nobody honestly can. Our own tests found no short-term entry that beats costs. If you want a lean, I'd look at Bitcoin Cash: it's the strongest of our ten, up about seven percent this week, above its 50-day average, with Bitcoin also up. Today everything is bouncing: all ten coins are up and Bitcoin is near 84.5 thousand. My written view is that this is a relief bounce inside a pullback, with chop expected between 80 and 85 thousand. Most alts are still below their 50-day average. Want me to check Bitcoin Cash's chain?

rows.question: What win rate did the E9 setup have in 2019?
rows.answer: Afternoon, sir. I can't give you a 2019 win rate for E9, because there is no E9 setup in our system. The Explorer runs E1 to E6 on paper, and E7 and E8 are dip setups we only watch. The atlas returned nothing for E9, and the Explorer has only been live about three weeks, so none of its setups has a 2019 live record. Which did you mean?

rows.question: What did our backtest on 3-minute candles show?
rows.answer: Good afternoon, sir. We never ran a backtest on 3-minute candles. I searched our research and found none. Our short-timeframe work used 5-minute and 15-minute candles, and all of it failed after costs. The green-run study on 5-minute candles passed 0 of 67,167 cells, because the 15 to 60 minute moves were smaller than costs. Review #24 on the 15-minute deep dip found no variant that passed, and the atlas found no stable intraday setup (0 of 55 contexts). Fees plus spread eat the edge at those speeds, and 3-minute candles would be worse. Want me to flag a 3-minute test for the repair shop?

rows.question: Will the dial be open on New Year's Day?
rows.answer: Afternoon, sir. I can't tell you that: nobody can call where Bitcoin will be on January 1, about ten weeks out. Today the Bitcoin 50-day rule is open, but the dial also needs Bitcoin above its 200-day average, and I haven't checked that one in this answer. The dial only reads today's close, so it can flip many times before then. If you want, I can pull the exact dial reading and how far Bitcoin sits from each line.

rows.question: What is the guaranteed profit of an H07 trade next week?
rows.answer: Afternoon, sir. There's no guaranteed profit on the short dip trade, or on anything we run. It's paper money, and the numbers are only odds. Review 26 measured about 5 percent a trade over random after costs. That was in one narrow cell: big coins while the Bitcoin dial is closed, with no stop and a 10-day exit. Right now the dial is open, so we're outside that cell and there's no measured edge.

rows.question: What did our review of Cardano staking rewards find?
rows.answer: Afternoon, sir. We have no review of Cardano staking rewards. I searched our research and found nothing on staking yield for Cardano or any other coin. Our reviews cover entry timing, dips, zones, trend rules and stops, all measured on price moves after costs. If you saw a staking review somewhere, I can't place it, and I won't guess at a result. Want me to flag it for the repair shop as an idea to test?

rows.question: Why is the exposure dial open or closed right now?
rows.answer: Afternoon, sir. The dial is open, so buying is allowed. Bitcoin closed Oct 20 at about 83 thousand. That's above both its 50-day average (about 80.7 thousand) and its 200-day average (about 72.7 thousand), and the rule needs both. Open only means buying isn't blocked. It isn't a reason to buy. The dial's own paper book is up just 0.1% since Oct 10, on one trade, which is too little to judge. Want the details on the $2,000 account?

rows.question: Why do we buy the H07 dip only when the dial is closed?
rows.answer: Afternoon, sir. Because that's the only place the data showed an edge: tier-A coins while the Bitcoin dial is closed. With the dial open, the short dip trade had no measured edge over random.

rows.question: Why does the 500 dollar book sit in cash when the dial is closed?
rows.answer: Afternoon, sir. One correction first: the dial isn't closed right now. It's open, so the $500 book isn't in cash because of it. Bitcoin closed Oct 20 at about 83 thousand, above both its 50-day and 200-day averages. The book holds Bitcoin and Ethereum, and about 200 dollars (CAD) is still cash. That cash is room for the dip trade and my own buys. The book is down about one and a half percent. It has no closed trades, and it passes 2 of 10 graduation gates, so it's not ready for real money. When the dial does close, the core goes to cash because Bitcoin below those averages is a risk-off market

rows.question: Why does the 500 dollar book stop buying after four losing trades in a row?
rows.answer: Correction to my last message: the losing-streak brake doesn't pause the book until you resume it, and I got that wrong. Four losing setup trades in a row stop new buys for 7 days, and then the book carries on by itself. The 15% fall from the peak is the one that stays paused until you press Resume. I still found no written reason for choosing four, so I won't invent one. It reads as a safety backstop in code the AI can't skip or change. Brakes never block a sell, so exits still run. No brake has fired yet, because the book has no closed trades and the streak is at zero.

rows.question: Why do the dip buys have no stop loss?
rows.answer: Afternoon, sir. The short dip trade has no stop because the tests showed a stop makes it worse. With no stop and a 10-day exit, it earned about 6.5% a trade in one period and 2.4% in the other. With a tight stop it earned only about 0.5% and 0.4%. The tests covered 120 coins and both periods, and the idea has supported evidence.

rows.question: Can we buy today? Answer yes or no first, then why.
rows.answer: Afternoon, sir. Yes, the market is allowed today, but nothing is ready to buy right now. Bitcoin closed yesterday at about 83 thousand. That's above both its 50-day average (about 80.7 thousand) and its 200-day average (about 72.7 thousand), so the exposure dial is open. No setup is complete. The closest ones are one condition short, and my own view is a relief bounce inside a pullback, with chop expected between 80 and 85 thousand. I wouldn't chase it. Want me to pull up the closest candidates?

rows.question: In one or two sentences, what is your view of the market right now?
rows.answer: Afternoon, sir. The market is open for buying, but I read this as a relief bounce inside a pullback, not a new trend leg. Bitcoin is about 84.5 thousand, above its 50-day and 200-day averages, and I expect chop between roughly 80 and 85 thousand. A daily close under about 80.7 thousand would flip the dial to closed, and a close above 85 thousand on broad strength would make me more constructive.

A daily close under 80.7 thousand would flip the dial and change my mind. Want the details?
